caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average change in INC score from the combined layer to the base layer, with gray bars representing inferred frames and orange bars representing lexical signal. The horizontal axis contains observation probabilities, labeled as 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9, with no specified scale type. The vertical axis, labeled "Average Change Using Compression," has a linear scale with a value range of -3 to 2, and units are not specified, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 1. The gray bars, representing inferred frames, have approximate values of -1.7, -1.5, -1.7, -1.2, -1.6, and -1.4. The orange bars, representing lexical signal, have approximate values of 0, 1, 2, 0.9, 1.1, and 1.1. The bars are grouped by observation probability, with no apparent sorting or visual emphasis.
